title: perf: overlap accepted private content compression with record writes
body:
## Problem

Jitendex's owned private content batches wait for compression before publishing references and encoding records. The current baseline already overlaps shared-buffer imports, but the private path still has this barrier.

## Change

After block compression has been selected, reuse the existing reserved-reference path for complete immutable private parser slabs. Metadata publication and record persistence can proceed while the same admitted batch compresses. The original source remains available for exact collision checks, cache adoption and worker-failure recovery, and the producer still waits for both operations before advancing.

The codec's compression bound is checked under the exclusive append owner. If the final cursor cannot be proved to fit below the existing 32-bit record representation limit, the same compression result uses the original suffix layout. The first private batch keeps measured compression selection. Worker counts, batch sizes, cache limits, compression settings and persistence formats are unchanged.

Accepted prefix placement intentionally relocates content references and resolved offset fields. Compressed frames, canonical content, prepared lookup keys, record partitions and total stored size remain unchanged. High-offset fallback preserves the original file bytes.

## Validation

- 521 focused tests across 10 suites; corrected reservation-table coverage also passes.
- Actual codec parity, canonical readback, mixed old/new references, record partitions and storage sizes; explicit >4 GiB suffix parity.
- Ownership, concurrent failure/drain, malformed reference callbacks, compression worker failures and terminal barriers.
- Main, test and dev TypeScript checks; scoped ESLint; all seven target dry builds.
- One concurrent typecheck was killed by the local host; its standalone rerun passed.

## Qualification

Frozen on develop `bbccabd520972cc351a65d9f545bd5369b6e9747`. Complete-import source comparisons and a separate process-tree memory study are being acquired. JMdict and VNDB are unchanged-path controls for this candidate. No full-import speedup is claimed yet; this remains a draft pending those results.

Original implementation; no third-party implementation code was copied.
